answer: In PoA, trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on the attestation graph: a node’s weight is the probability mass reaching it from trusted seeds. A sybil cluster hidden behind a sparse cut has low conductance, so few walks enter it before termination; min-cut and transitivity bounds constrain its aggregate voting weight by boundary flow, not internal size. Thus karst, pigment, and dune identities cannot amplify influence without trusted cross-links.
